title: Todd H NDE
content:
Was beginning my second round of palliative chemotherapy. Steroids and anti-nausea had been given via IV. Docetaxel chemotherapy was administered. Flow had commenced about 3-4 minutes. I was aware something was wrong. I was able to get a nurses attention. The nurse quickly removed the IV. A nursing team of 4 or 5 began working on me, administered an antidote. It is the time frame between removing the IV, and the antidote taking hold, that I began my experience.

I felt myself being pulled away and I was leaving my body. I was clear headed, but unable to verbally communicate. I felt a narrowing of both, my vision and my spatial awareness. The feeling of leaving was overwhelming; overwhelming is not exactly the right term, but it will do. I had a physical sensation of being pulled away from behind my body, by my chest and shoulders. I could see and hear what was happening in front of me with extreme clarity. I was aware of staff working on me, moving my body to a more reclining position, and talking to me. My mind told me to answer, but I was physically unable to do so. I was sad. I was dying and felt alone.

The antidote took hold quickly and my spatial awareness opened up. Before, I was focused on the small area in front of me. Now, I could hear in the room and my peripheral vision was restored. The antidote made me feel stoned. I was also physically shaking and trembling. After some time, the ability to speak, move, and walk returned. When I was able, my wife took me home.

I was reliving the experience over and over, and finally was able to sleep. When I woke, I was clear in my thoughts about what had happened. I had begun the near death experience. I had stepped into the doorway of the other side, but had not ventured any further down the path.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes Allergic Reaction. Life threatening event, but not clinical death. Undergoing palliative chemotherapy, stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal. I had focus and clarity like I've never had before
elements.At what time during the experience were: When the chemo was stopped, before the antidote was administered
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning. Events were happening. I cannot tell you how long they took
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: My vision was narrowed, but sharp. It was like looking through an undistorted magnifying glass.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: Focused on the area I could see. No peripheral hearing
elements.Did you pass into or through a tunnel?: Uncertain. It was as though had this gone any further, I would be passing through the tunnel.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience. I had no definite beliefs
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Uncertain. It is something I think about a lot.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I do not know how my remembrance of the experience compares to my remembrance of other life events that occurred around the time of the experience
elements.Have you ever shared this experience wit: Yes 9 hours. My wife acknowledged it.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Uncertain The usual information everyone has
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real. Because it happened.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real. It happened
